::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** Oct 26th 1866  
**From:** Elderfield, Otterbourne, Winchester.  
**Manuscript:** MS British Library Add MSS 54920: 164-165
:::

Dear [Mr Macmillan](people/person_939.qmd),
Can you tell me how far back in time the reservation of the right of translation goes-? There is a pretty story of Paul Feval’s in the <u>[Feé des Grèves](other_books/otherbook_471.qmd)</u> which [my mother](people/person_1606.qmd) translated, and I want to have in the [Monthly Packet](organizations/other_52.qmd).[^1] It was printed in 1853, and is out of print in France, and there is no notice of reservation of translation in the title page - however by way of being on the safe side I wrote to ask for authorisation for the translation, and this morning my letter has been returned to me with these incomprehensible marks on the envelope. Now if 1853 was - (as I rather think) before it became necessary to get leave to translate, there need by no more trouble, but if not perhaps you could tell me how to make a less unsuccessful application. Whether M. Dageneau has removed - or who is M. Févals present publisher.[^2] The story ought to begin in January so I am rather anxious about it.

[Miss Sewell](people/person_1301.qmd) is coming here today for a consultation over the extracts. I think we have nearly enough in bulk for a first [volume](cmy_books/cmybook_71.qmd), but there are two or three important bits for which we have not yet found writing interesting enough - the Battle of the Standard <sup>3</sup>- Magna Carta, and all Henry II that was not either Becket or Ireland especially.

I am going to send you a piece of [Miss Peard](people/person_1160.qmd)’s work for the [Sunday Library](organizations/other_145.qmd) in a few days.

Yours sincerely
C M Yonge

---

[^1]: It appeared as 'The Fairy of the Sands'. It seems that CMY was mistaken in thinking Dagneau's 1853 edition was the first.
[^2]: The Battle of the Standard (1138), between the Scots and the English, at Northallerton in North Yorkshire.
